text: By 2004, LEGO had invented thousands of new pieces. And most of them were used in exactly one set.
That same year, the company behind the world's most famous toy lost almost two billion Danish kroner. About three hundred million dollars.
Those two facts are connected. And the man who would have to untangle them was thirty-five years old, and had joined LEGO only three years earlier, from a consulting firm.
To see how a box of bricks nearly sank its own maker, you have to start with one word that LEGO lived by. System.
